@emmanuelbernard is this native build ? 

It seems you send a request with `Accept: application/json`so the NotFoundExceptionMapper try to generate a json representation but fails as no json provider is found. If you use the `reasteasy-jsonb` extension this should works.

Well, it's more complex than that. I fixed a bug where we had a resource locator instead of a resource method. Then I fixed a bug with the way variants were selected. But now I'm getting exceptions like:

```
org.jboss.resteasy.spi.UnhandledException: org.jboss.resteasy.core.NoMessageBodyWriterFoundFailure: Could not find MessageBodyWriter for response object of type: java.lang.String of media type: text/html;charset=UTF-8
```

And frankly that's just plain weird.

Oh, I bet I know. It's because we only register the providers if there's a method annotated with `@Path`, I'm sure. Because the minute I put at least one method, it works. 

The fact that jsonb is a required dep is another issue.
Or it's because we don't find any method returning that MIME type so the media writers are removed.

OK, that's it: we only register message body writers for method return types we find, so if we don't have any REST method defined, we don't register message body writers for `String` or for JSON (regardless of whether the `resteasy-jsonb` dependency is present).

So that solves the super weird behaviour.

@gsmet since you did the provider scanning, what do you think of forcing `String` message body writers in every case?

Now, in the case of the JSON error mapper it's more complex, because even if I force the JSON body writer (I'd have to know which one), it still won't work without a json serialiser present. I can't make resteasy depend on `resteasy-jsonb`, so we're left with either simplifying the JSON error down to some really simple JSON representation (we can skip the list of existing resources), or using own own String->JSON builder, or doing it manually, or removing the JSON error entirely.

WDYT?

Could we raise a deployment exception when an app has app/JSON endpoints
but not RESTEasy-JSON or Jackson ?

@emmanuelbernard I think it's the opposite :) we should raise a deployment exception when an app has resteasy-jsonb or resteasy-jackson but no endpoint ... Or just a runtime exception as with livereload we tend to launch the app early in the developement process.

@FroMage I think that generating an exception / a warning to give the developer a hint of what happens is enought for the moment. When the Vert.x works will be finihsed, all exception pages should be revisited (ongoing discussions on #3646 ) and we can decide then if we want to implements them via basic string concatenation ...
